title: GO:0015343    siderophore-iron transmembrane transporter activity PANTHER:PTN001160847

author: ValWood
body:
There are two different types of native siderophore transporters:
Exporters – that secrete the native siderophore into the environment.
Importers – that import the iron-siderophore complex back into the cell.

these appear to be 'native' transporters  but they are labelled 
Siderophore iron transporter mirA in uniprot

@marcfeuermann @Antonialock  how do we get this fixed?

author: marcfeuermann
body:
**GO:0015343 siderophore-iron transmembrane transporter activity** is a parent of  **GO:0042931: enterobactin transmembrane transporter activity**.  MirA is indeed a enterobactin transporter.
Q8X1Z7 is annotated from PMID:12487628 (in GO by AspGD, in UniProt and subsequently in PAN-GO)
MirA is specific for enterobactin which is not a native siderophore. 
**"MIRA transports specifically the heterologous siderophore enterobactin and that MIRB transports exclusively the native siderophore triacetylfusarinine C"**
There is also some evidence for the pombe sequences from PMID:12888492 to confirm the PAN-GO annotation:
**"Str1 is a S.pombe siderophore‐iron transporter"**
As things stand, all this seems correct to me. 
I see that an ontology issue is open (https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29742), but the available evidence still favors the siderophore-iron transmembrane transporter activity (even if you separate the native exporter activity).
I could remove the annotation, but need a good reason to do it.
Sorry if I missed something here.
Cheers,
Marc.
